messages.subject: Vector/matrix multiplication in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

i am a little confused with vector/matrix multiplication in R;

say:

p=c(1,2)
e=c(3,3)

then

p*e returns element-wise multiplication of p,e;
t(p)*e also returns ement-wise multiplication of p,e (true?) (and, is
there any other wat to transpose a vector?);
how do you matrix-multiply p,e? (that is, t(p) and e, assuming each of
p,e are treated as column vectors..)

Thanks,

Asaf

messages.subject: Re: Vector/matrix multiplication in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi Asaf,
Here are some examples for you

a=c(1,2)
b=c(3,3)

a*b
a*t(b)
t(a)*b

a%*%b
a%*%t(b)
t(a)%*%b

messages.subject: Re: ועוד אתגר
messages.body_plain:
list.files(pattern = 'raw')

if you want to do the same for a different directory

list.files(path = "c:\\path\\to\\data\\", pattern = "raw")

the parameter "pattern" is a regular expression so you can use its for a much more clever matching scheme:

file that start with "raw": pattern = "^raw"
files that end with "raw": pattern = "raw$"
etc....

reps<- 100000
save.1<- function(replications){
  .result<- vector('list', length=replications)
  for (i in 1:replications){ .result[i]<-rnorm(1)}
return(.result)
}

system.time(save.1(reps))

save.2<- function(replications){
  .result<- list()
  for (i in 1:replications){ .result[i]<-rnorm(1) }
return(.result)
}

system.time(save.2(reps))

# Rosette:
n = 17
theta = seq(0, 2 * pi, length = n + 1)[1:n]
x = sin(theta)
y = cos(theta)
(v1 = rep(1:n, n))
(v2 = rep(1:n, rep(n, n)))
plot.new <http://plot.new>()
plot.window(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), asp = 1)
segments(x[v1], y[v1], x[v2], y[v2])
box()

# Curve Enveloppe:
x1 = seq(0, 1, length = 20)
y1 = rep(0, 20)
x2 = rep(0, 20)
y2 = seq(0.75, 0, length = 20)
plot.new <http://plot.new>()
plot.window(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 0.75), asp = 1)
segments(x1, y1, x2, y2)
box(col = "grey")

--
